advisory.finding: The all-or-nothing 'nothing recorded' contract on rebar.attach_commits is not tested end-to-end: no test drives the seam with a bad SHA and asserts it raises RebarError AND leaves the ticket's recorded commits unchanged. Only the low-level helper invalid_commit_shas is tested (it returns the list of bad SHAs), which does not verify the batch is rejected before any COMMITS event is appended.
scenarios: A regression that appends the valid records before validating (or on a partial-validation bug) would leave a half-linked ticket — the exact failure the commit message says the design prevents — and no test would catch it.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm merge commits that introduce their own changes cannot bypass the file-impact-vs-diff check when their parents don't independently reference the ticket.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:265: `if commit_impact.is_merge_commit(sha, code_root): continue  # a merge authors nothing of its own; its parents are scanned instead`
commit_impact.py:101-116 is_merge_commit returns True on >2 rev-list tokens with no inspection of whether the merge introduced content

The 'its parents are scanned in their own right' rationale only holds if the parents themselves reference/are-attached-to the ticket; a merge whose parents carry no trailer leaves its own diff unexamined.
dropped.finding: A merge commit that is itself a referencing commit (references the ticket via trailer) is skipped by is_merge_commit before its changed paths are ever read. If such a merge introduces changes of its own (a non-trivial/'evil' merge, or a squash landed as a merge) and its parents do NOT independently reference the ticket or appear as attached SHAs, those undeclared paths are never verified against file_impact — the check silently passes.
scenarios: A referencing merge commit that resolves conflicts by editing an undeclared source file, whose parents do not reference the ticket.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `attached` should count newly-added SHAs (post-dedup) rather than submitted SHAs, given the new CLI print and idempotency claim.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:734: `return {"ticket_id": tid, "attached": len(records)}`
src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py: `print(f"ATTACHED: {result['attached']} commit(s) to {result['ticket_id']}")`
docs/mcp-reference.md: `Retroactively link commits to a ticket by SHA (union-add, idempotent).`
dropped.finding: The `attached` count returned by rebar.attach_commits is len(records) — the number of SHAs submitted — not the number newly added after union-merge dedup. The CLI prints `ATTACHED: {result['attached']} commit(s)` and docs describe the op as 'idempotent (union-add)', so re-attaching an already-linked SHA reports it as attached, misrepresenting a no-op as a mutation.
scenarios: Re-running attach-commits with a SHA already recorded reports 'ATTACHED: 1 commit(s)' though nothing changed.
